result.text: Week 12 ACR20 response: OLUMIANT 2 mg 49% vs placebo 27% (treatment difference 22; 95% CI 12, 32).

indication.text: OLUMIANT (baricitinib) is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF antagonist therapies.

citations.quote: OLUMIANT® (baricitinib) is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more tumor necrosis factor (TNF) antagonist therapies.

target_moa.text: Baricitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor; JAKs are intracellular enzymes that transmit cytokine/growth-factor signals and phosphorylate STATs, and baricitinib had greater inhibitory potency at JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 relative to JAK3.

citations.quote: Baricitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor. JAKs are intracellular enzymes which transmit signals arising from cytokine or growth factor-receptor interactions on the cellular membrane to influence cellular processes of hematopoiesis and immune cell function.
In cell-free isolated enzyme assays, baricitinib had greater inhibitory potency at JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 relative to JAK3.

modality.text: Small molecule (oral JAK inhibitor; molecular weight 371.42).

citations.quote: OLUMIANT (baricitinib) is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor with the chemical name {1-(ethylsulfonyl)-3-[4-(7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4-yl)-1H-pyrazol-1-yl]azetidin-3-yl}acetonitrile. Baricitinib has an empirical formula of C16H17N7O2S and a molecular weight of 371.42.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): upper respiratory tract infections (16.3% with 2 mg vs 11.7% placebo), nausea (2.7% vs 1.6%), herpes simplex, and herpes zoster. Serious risks include serious infections, malignancy, and thrombosis (during the 16-week period venous thromboses occurred in 5 patients on baricitinib 4 mg vs 0 on placebo).

detail.text: Boxed warning for SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MALIGNANCY, AND THROMBOSIS: serious infections leading to hospitalization or death (including tuberculosis and bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, and other opportunistic infections); lymphoma and other malignancies; and thrombosis, including deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism observed at increased incidence versus placebo.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MALIGNANCY, AND THROMBOSIS

- Serious infections leading to hospitalization or death, including tuberculosis and bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, and other opportunistic infections, have occurred in patients receiving OLUMIANT. (5.1)
Lymphoma and other malignancies have been observed in patients treated with OLUMIANT [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.2)].
Thrombosis, including deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, has been observed at an increased incidence in patients treated with OLUMIANT compared to placebo.

vote.text: An Arthritis Advisory Committee was convened on April 23, 2018; it voted 10 Yes, 5 No that the benefit-risk profile was adequate to support approval of baricitinib 2 mg, and 5 Yes, 10 No for the 4 mg dose.

citations.quote: An Arthritis Advisory Committee (AAC) was convened on April 23, 2018 to discuss this NDA.1 The following is a brief summary of the voting and discussion from the AAC meeting.

7. **VOTE (Benefit/Risk 2 mg):** Is the benefit-risk profile adequate to support approval of baricitinib 2 mg for the proposed indication of the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response or are intolerant to methotrexate (MTX)?

- If no, what data are needed?
- 10 Yes, 5 No, 0 Abstain

- If no, what data are needed?
- 5 Yes, 10 No, 0 Abstain
- There is a need for more data. Several panelists did note that benefit/risk could be acceptable for a refractory population.

detail.text: Not a first-cycle approval; the original NDA received a Complete Response action on April 12, 2017 because the overall benefit-risk assessment of baricitinib 2 mg and 4 mg once daily was not favorable, and the application was resubmitted as a complete response dated December 4, 2017.

citations.quote: The original NDA for baricitinib was submitted on January 14, 2016. Safety concerns were identified, including the risk of venous thrombosis, and the application received a Complete Response (CR) action on April 12, 2017 because the overall benefit-risk assessment of baricitinib 2 mg and 4 mg once daily was not favorable.
We acknowledge receipt of your amendment dated December 4, 2017, which constituted a complete response to our April 12, 2017, action letter.

requirement.text: PMR 3421-1: Randomized controlled clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety of baricitinib in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, including two doses of baricitinib and an active comparator, sufficient to evaluate arterial and venous thrombosis, cardiovascular adverse events, opportunistic infections, and malignancy.

citations.quote: 3421-1 Randomized controlled clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety of baricitinib in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The trial will include two doses of baricitinib and an active comparator. The trial should be of sufficient size and duration to evaluate safety events of interest, including arterial and venous thrombosis, cardiovascular adverse events, opportunistic infections, and malignancy.

summary.text: The original NDA for baricitinib was submitted January 15, 2016 and received a Complete Response action on April 12, 2017 due to unfavorable benefit-risk (venous thrombosis risk); Lilly resubmitted a complete response dated December 4, 2017. An Arthritis Advisory Committee convened on April 23, 2018, and the 2 mg dose was approved with a boxed warning and a required long-term safety postmarketing trial.
